svg.title: GraphQL Federation
svg.desc: GraphQL Federation. Subgraphs from many services compose into one graph; a router plans each query across them. Step 1, One graph, many teams: Each team publishes its subgraph; composition merges them into one supergraph or fails the build. Step 2, Router plans each query: One query, one endpoint: Products first, then Reviews and Inventory in parallel by key, then merge. Step 3, Checked before they ship: Removing rating would break the mobile app's query, so the check blocks it; adding stars ships. Step 4, Know the costs: Mind hops, N+1, costly queries, authorisation and the router; a failed subgraph gives partial data.

g.text: Each team publishes its subgraph; composition merges them into one supergraph or fails the build.
One query, one endpoint: Products first, then Reviews and Inventory in parallel by key, then merge.
Removing rating would break the mobile app's query, so the check blocks it; adding stars ships.
Mind hops, N+1, costly queries, authorisation and the router; a failed subgraph gives partial data.
checks run in each subgraph's build;
only changes that pass are published
Products, Reviews and Inventory compose into one supergraph, and the router loads it
Inventory's change adds Product.price as String; Products defines it as Float!
composition fails in Inventory's build: nothing is deployed, the router keeps its supergraph
supergraph in use: Products v41 + Reviews v12 + Inventory v8
the router answers every query from this one composed schema
removing Review.rating still composes, but the mobile app's query reads it
operation check against the last 7 days of traffic: breaking, so the build is blocked
adding Review.stars composes and breaks no operation: Reviews ships v13 on its own
splits each query by which subgraph
